idea-plugin.name: Relay
idea-plugin.description:
Relay sends editor context to a configurable coding agent in a dedicated terminal tab. Works with Cursor, Claude Code, Aider, and any CLI agent you configure.

Features

  • Agent library — save agents with name, command, reference mode, and launch mode
  • Goose-aware references — interactive Goose/TUI sessions use @path; batch CLI keeps Read path
  • Default agent — shortcuts always open Relay:<default> and run that agent's command
  • Quick default switch — change the default from Relay → Default Agent in the editor menu
  • Agent-native file references — @path for Cursor/Claude, /add path for Aider, or Read path for other agents
  • Agent-native selections — line-range @ syntax for Cursor/Claude, or fenced snippets with file and line references for other agents
  • Focus existing tab — reuses and focuses the tab instead of opening a duplicate
  • Customizable shortcuts — change keyboard shortcuts from plugin settings or Settings → Keymap
  • Cross-IDE support — PyCharm, WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, and other IDEs with the Terminal plugin (2025.3+)

Default keyboard shortcuts

  • Ctrl+Alt+T — Open or focus Relay
  • Ctrl+Alt+P — Send file path to Relay
  • Ctrl+Alt+Enter — Send selection (with file path and lines) to Relay

Configure agents under Settings → Tools → Relay. Switch the default quickly from the editor menu: Relay → Default Agent.

How to switch the default agent

  1. Right-click in the editor → Relay → Default Agent
  2. Pick an agent (checkmark shows the current default)
  3. Use any Relay shortcut — the next trigger opens Relay:<agent> and runs that agent's command

Example agents

  • Cursor — name: cursor, command: agent
  • Claude Code — name: claude, command: claude
  • Aider — name: aider, command: aider --model sonnet
